body:
Local browser matches currently tie drawing and input to the 25 Hz simulation clock, and accelerated ticks pay for a separate nested timer. This change draws and consumes input on animation-frame callbacks, batches due ticks within a 6 ms work slice, reduces synchronous DOM crossings, and makes WebGL error polling opt-in. Paused local maps repaint less often. Relay matches preserve their existing polling, catch-up and drawing cadence.

The implementation shares drawing and session-failure handling, documents the host scheduling contract, and retains a reusable opt-in profiling harness. Resize requests survive WebGL context loss, including restoration while the tab remains hidden. Gradient SIMD experiments are excluded: the measured candidates regressed large fields.

### Feel and performance

The retained investigation on Apple M3 / Chromium / ANGLE Metal observed normal serial presentation rising from ~25 to ~60 FPS and 8× throughput from ~120 to ~200 ticks/sec on `games/gd-bigarena-long.game.gz`. Paused serial CPU fell from ~35% to ~29% of one core. Active-play CPU increased with the extra rendering; this PR does **not** claim an overall CPU reduction. Concurrent workloads limit the precision of these timings. Those comparative captures precede integration with current master. A capture at `d016b4ea5` maintains ~60 serial draw FPS and ~200 ticks/sec at 8×; all timed captures predate the final `a23089cb3` integration and remain affected by concurrent workloads.

### Verification

- Sub-agent review identified allocation-failure translation and hidden-tab restoration bugs; both were corrected. The final review, including integration with master at `a23089cb3`, has no remaining findings and confirms relay scheduling is preserved.
- 34 browser unit checks, 286 build-system checks (one skip), and 13 browser-package contracts pass.
- Native ARM syntax checks pass for the changed engine and screen sources.
- Previous prototype validation: 15 targeted Chromium cases, serial/threaded hosted 1,500-tick traces matching the baseline, and 1,008 gradient oracle cases.
- The `web-package web-tests` build at `dbfa56cb9` passes. 27 Chromium regressions pass, covering serial/threaded pacing under WebGL and software rendering, resize, repeated context loss/hidden restoration, save persistence, replay verification and loader transitions. The real-UI 1,500-tick traces match the headless reference.
- CI exposed missing dependencies in the existing native online probes. Both probes now share their no-game-data file-manager helper and link their TCP/SHA/version dependencies; both link and start locally. The reviewer checked this follow-up and found no remaining issues.
- Final integration also exposed a scene-boundary violation in an upstream change. The unchanged telemetry display-value type now lives in a shared data header; Scene headers remain independent of the live telemetry sink. The sub-agent reviewed this cleanup without findings.
- The final integration preserves upstream gameplay recording: threaded drawing supplies tick and timing metadata from the exact immutable Scene being rendered. The sub-agent reviewed this integration without findings.
- Latest master integration at `7123176e7` also passes the complete browser build and repeats the four affected WebGL pacing/context cases, two software pacing cases, native syntax/probe checks and build-system/browser units. Four isolated worker packaging smoke cases pass. The upstream telemetry cleanup is retained; a duplicate native probe stub introduced upstream now uses the shared helper. Independent review has no findings.
- Hosted CI remains backlogged. The maintainer explicitly approved merging with passing relevant local checks. Full native/mobile gameplay equivalence has not been established locally; native syntax and probe builds provide narrower coverage.

[Review evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/browser-performance-evidence) includes profiles, fixture/runtime hashes, 1,500-tick traces, screenshots, commands, build/test logs, gradient oracle results and sub-agent feedback. Temporary experiments and benchmark dumps are excluded from the production diff.
title: Improve local browser frame pacing and accelerated simulation
